title: Confucius (Kong Qiu)
subtitle: A historical figure of classical education, ritual and political ethics
shortSummary: Confucius is a recognisable gateway into Confucian classics, education and political ethics; sayings in the Analects must be separated from disciple records, compilation layers and later classical reception.
curatorialDescription: The historical-person layer can connect Confucius with the House of Confucius in the Shiji, the Zhou rites-asking narrative and teaching activity, while the Analects remains a composite text of transmitted sayings.

From Confucius to Kong Yingda, the museum presents a long chain of person, speech, compilation and institutional reception rather than projecting Tang classical learning back onto Confucius as direct participation.
researchNote: Confucius has an early historiographical record. The Analects is a composite transmitted text; saying relations are marked recorded_by_others, while Tang institutional reception is modelled separately.
